summary: ADR-033 cites docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md, which does not exist (TKT-128 incidental)
description:
### Finding (incidental, surfaced during TKT-128 implementation)

`docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md:237` cites:

```
- `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` — recommendation R3, the originating finding
```

**That file does not exist.** Not on `main`, not on the `arch-review-in-place` branch, not anywhere
in history (`git log --all --diff-filter=A -- 'docs/reviews/*'` is empty; `docs/reviews/` is not a
directory in this repo). The 2026-07-25 architecture review was conducted in-session and its
recommendations were written straight into tickets (R3 → TKT-126/ADR-033, R4 → TKT-128), never into
a review file.

So an ADR's References section points a reader at provenance they cannot open. AGENTS.md says
documentation is 100% in-repo; a dead in-repo path is worse than no path, because it reads as if the
evidence exists somewhere.

### Why this is a separate ticket

Found while implementing TKT-128, which had the *same* dead link in its own ticket references.
TKT-128 avoided reproducing it (its ADR-004 amendment cites TKT-128/TKT-31 instead), but fixing
ADR-033 was outside its COS and would have been scope creep in a docs-only PR whose COS 5 pins the
diff to two files.

### Two ways to close it — decide, don't assume

1. **Re-point the citation** (smallest): ADR-033 cites TKT-126 for provenance, as ADR-004 now does
   for TKT-128. Reversible, no new artifact.
2. **Write the review file** the citations assume: reconstruct `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md`
   from the R1–Rn findings now living on the board. Bigger, and only worth it if the review has
   standing value beyond the tickets it spawned.

Recommendation: option 1 unless the owner wants the review preserved as a document.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] No ADR references a path that does not exist in the repo.
- [ ] `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` either returns nothing, or every hit resolves to a real file.
- [ ] Docs-only; no source changes.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — branch `TKT-136-adr-033-dead-citation` off `origin/main` @ 8789b1c

**Selection reason:** the owner named this ticket for a fully autonomous end-to-end run. It is the
right shape for one: docs-only, `risk:low`, one AC that a grep decides, and the single design
decision (option 1 vs option 2) was already taken at shaping — so an autonomous run makes no
product choice a human hasn't already made.

**Blockers:** none. Both links are `relates` (TKT-126, TKT-128); no `blocks` edge exists.

**Finding re-verified at claim time**, not trusted from the ticket: `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/`
at `origin/main` (8789b1c) returns exactly one hit —
`docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md:237`. `docs/reviews/` is not a directory in the
repo. The ticket was shaped against a stale local checkout of `main`; ADR-033 itself only landed in
8789b1c, so the citation and the ADR arrived together.

---

### ⚠️ Gate waiver — this ticket ran gateless, by explicit owner instruction

The repo owner waived **all four human gates** for this run as a deliberate process experiment, and
asked that the waiver be recorded here so the board history shows it. Recorded verbatim in effect:

| Gate | Normally | This run |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — priority | human moves Backlog → Ready | already satisfied; the ticket was in `Ready` at claim |
| 2 — plan approval | human moves Planning → Building | **waived** — also already skipped by `risk:low`. Open decisions resolved by the agent: prefer the plan-critique's recommendation, else the most reversible option. Every self-made decision is recorded in `kind=plan-final`. |
| 3 — review + merge | human reviews the PR and squash-merges | **waived** — the agent squash-merges after the adversarial ai-review converges (same triage, second-pass and churn-cap rules). The review-guide is still posted on the PR first, as the audit record. |
| 4 — PO acceptance | PO validates COS and moves to Done | **waived** — the agent self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code, posts the validation note, and closes with the full metrics comment. |

**Unchanged and non-negotiable for this run:** `config.models` routing with no substitutions
(plan → `gpt-5.6-sol`, planReview → main-agent, implement → main-agent, aiReview → `gpt-5.6-sol`);
cross-model review for both the plan and the code; TDD with tests observed red first; `make check`
green before every push and again after the merge; every marker comment posted at its stage; no AI
attribution in any commit or PR.

**Standing stop conditions** (agent halts and reports instead of proceeding): the gate or CI fails
twice on the same cause with no clear fix; the work would touch auth, money paths, data migrations
or CI/deploy config in a way the plan did not anticipate; a blocking review finding survives the
churn cap; a configured model is unreachable after the escalation ladder; or a destructive,
hard-to-reverse action with an ambiguous right answer.

**What the waiver does not change:** the risk that gates exist to catch. `risk:low` is
challengeable — if this stops being a docs-only one-line diff, the label comes off and the run
stops for a human.

→ `Ready` → `Planning`, label `agent:planning`.

### Plan draft — written by `gpt-5.6-sol` (config.models.plan), via the codex companion `task`, effort high, read-only (no `--write`), 1m11s

Reproduced verbatim below. Attribution: this is the drafter's output, not mine; the critique
follows under `agent:plan-review`.

---

## DoD

- Remove the nonexistent `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` reference from ADR-033.
- Preserve the existing TKT-126 reference as the provenance pointer.
- `! grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` exits successfully.

- `docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md`
  - Delete the final References bullet containing the dead review path.
  - Do not add a replacement: the first References bullet already cites TKT-126, which carries the

## Test plan

Use the COS-2 grep as the executable TDD seam; do not commit a checker.

1. Before editing, run `! grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/`. Observe exit status 1 and the ADR-033:237 hit.
2. Delete the dead citation.
3. Run the same command and observe exit status 0 with no output. Record the red/green evidence in the PR.
4. Verify scope and repository health: `git diff --check`, `git diff --name-only`, `make check`.

A committed link checker would require at least a new script and a `Makefile` change, violating the
docs-only scope and shortest-diff rule. Adding an unproven repository-wide gate could also surface
unrelated legacy citations across all ADRs and expand this ticket into link-cleanup work.

## Risks

- Deleting the line could appear to lose provenance. Mitigation: ADR-033 already names TKT-126 in
  its first References bullet, and that ticket contains fuller context.
- The standard gate has no documentation-link stage. Mitigation: preserve the targeted red-then-green
  command as explicit PR evidence.
- A broader checker could create unrelated failures. Mitigation: do not add or wire one in this ticket.

none

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan-final -->
### Plan-final — delta on the `kind=plan` draft. Critique by **main-agent** (`config.models.planReview`; drafter was `gpt-5.6-sol`, so the cross-model pair holds).

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Not restated here.

---

## 1. The draft's premise is false, and so is the ticket's — `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` exists

The ticket says the file "does not exist. Not on `main`, not on the `arch-review-in-place` branch,
not anywhere in history." The first two clauses are right and the conclusion drawn from them is
wrong. What is actually true:

```
$ ls -la docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md
.rw-r--r--@ 10.0k matdupui 25 Jul 11:26 2026-07-25-architecture.md

$ git check-ignore -v docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md
.gitignore:15:docs/reviews/	docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md

$ git ls-tree -r HEAD --name-only | grep -c docs/reviews
0
```

The review is a real, finished, ~10k document sitting in the working tree — it opens *"# Architecture
Review / Date: 2026-07-25 / Scope: Full codebase — 5 Go services + gateway + 3 web apps, ~24k prod
LOC…"* and its body is the R1–Rn findings this ADR and TKT-128 came from. It is absent from the repo
because **`.gitignore:15` excludes `docs/reviews/`**, not because it was never written.

Nobody was wrong to file the ticket — a reader of the repo genuinely cannot open that path, which is
the defect. But three downstream statements in the thread are wrong and are corrected here, because
the thread is the memory:

- the ticket's *"never into a review file"* — it was written into a review file;
- the shaping comment's *"reconstructing `docs/reviews/…` … the review has no standing value"* —
  reconstruction was never needed, and "standing value" was judged against a document nobody had read;
- **my own `kind=claim` comment's** *"`docs/reviews/` is not a directory in the repo"* — it is a
  directory in the working tree, ignored by git. `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` missed it only
  because the review's text does not happen to contain the string `docs/reviews`.

**Why this did not change the chosen approach:** it changes the *reason* for the fix, not the fix.
An ignored file is not in the repo; a reader cloning this repo still cannot open that path;
`AGENTS.md`'s "documentation is 100% in-repo" is still violated by citing it. Option 1 (re-point)
remains correct and remains the most reversible option. What the discovery *does* raise — should
`docs/reviews/` be gitignored at all, given that house rule? — is a **decision**, and decisions are
tickets, not commits. Filed as a follow-up (§4); explicitly **not** taken in this run.

## 2. Per-part verdicts on the draft

| Draft element | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Touch only `docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md` | **accept** | Verified at HEAD: `git grep -n "docs/reviews" HEAD -- docs/` returns that one line, 237. |
| COS-2 grep as the TDD seam, red-then-green, nothing new committed | **accept** | Correct call. It is executable, it is red now, and it is the AC verbatim. |
| Do not commit a link checker | **accept, reasoning corrected** | Conclusion right, evidence wrong — see §3. The load-bearing reason is COS 3 (docs-only; no source changes), not "it would surface legacy citations". |
| "Delete the final References bullet; do not add a replacement" | **amend → re-point, don't delete** | Two reasons. (a) **Owner's shaping decision was option 1, "re-point the citation at TKT-126"** — that is a human decision already taken, not an open one, and a waived Gate 2 does not license reversing it. (b) On the merits: the review/R3 provenance appears **nowhere else** in ADR-033 — `grep -n -i "review" ADR-033` shows the other five hits are all about the *adversarial code review*, a different thing. The first bullet ("TKT-126 — this ticket") records *which ticket*, never *that an architecture review's R3 originated it*. Deleting the line loses that fact permanently; re-pointing costs one line and keeps it. |
| DoD item "`git diff --check` and `make check` pass" | **accept** | Kept, and `make check` is mandatory before push per the run's terms. |
| "Open decisions: none" | **reject** | There was one the drafter could not see, because my brief handed it the false premise. Resolved in §4. |

## 3. Correcting the draft's evidence about a repo-wide link checker

The draft asserted a checker "could surface unrelated legacy citations across all ADRs". I tested
both matchers rather than repeating the claim:

- **Naive matcher** (any backticked `*.md|go|ts|sql|…` token or markdown link): **35 unresolved hits
  across 36 ADR files** — but essentially all are bare filenames used as prose (`consumer.go`,
  `store.go`, `src/fetch.ts`, `0003_lifecycle_integrity.sql`), never intended as repo paths. Those
  are not defects, they are how the ADRs are written.
- **Repo-rooted matcher** (path's first segment is a real top-level dir): **0 dead citations across
  all of `docs/`** — other than the one this ticket is about.

So the draft's stated risk is real only for a matcher too crude to ship, and its conclusion survives
for a different reason. One extra finding falls out of this, and it is the sharpest argument against
a committed checker: because the review file **exists locally and is gitignored**, a link checker run
here would go **green on this very defect**, and red only in CI or a fresh clone. A gate that
disagrees with itself depending on whose machine it runs on is worse than no gate. If a checker is
ever wanted, it must resolve paths against `git ls-files`, not the filesystem — noted in the
follow-up, not built here.

## 4. Decisions I took myself (Gate 2 waived by the owner) — and why

Recorded per the run's terms: prefer what the critique recommends; absent a recommendation, take the
most reversible option.

**D1 — Re-point the citation rather than delete it.** *Critique recommendation (§2), and it restores
the owner's own shaping decision.* One line, reversible, keeps provenance. Exact replacement for
line 237:

```
- The 2026-07-25 architecture review, recommendation R3 — the originating finding. The review is not
  an in-repo document; its recommendations live on the board (R3 → TKT-126, R4 → TKT-128).
```

Every clause is verifiable from the repo: no path, no dead link, and it stops implying an openable
artifact. It says "not an in-repo document" rather than "was never written", because the latter is
the falsehood §1 just corrected — the fix must not replace a dead pointer with a wrong sentence.

**D2 — Do not commit the ignored review file, and do not touch `.gitignore`.** *Most-reversible
rule.* Committing a 10k document the owner deliberately excluded is the least reversible option on
the table (it enters history), it is outside COS 3 (docs-only… but this ticket's docs are ADRs, not a
new artifact), and the ignore rule's intent is undocumented — `docs/reviews/` sits in `.gitignore`'s
"build artifacts & dependencies" block with no explanatory comment, unlike `spike/` and
`.plan-brief.*` which both carry one. That is precisely the ambiguity a human should resolve.

**D3 — File the discovery as a new backlog ticket, don't fold it in.** Standard incidental triage.
The ticket to file: *"`docs/reviews/` is gitignored but holds a real architecture review — decide
whether it belongs in-repo"*, citing the `AGENTS.md` documentation-in-repo rule, and noting the
`git ls-files`-vs-filesystem trap from §3 for any future link checker.

**D4 — One commit, no ADR amendment block.** ADR-033 is being corrected, not amended: the decision it
records is untouched, only a broken reference to it. An `## Amendment` section (as ADR-004 carries for
TKT-128) would overstate what happened.

## 5. Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

Per the cross-model rule, these were **added** by the critique rather than accepted/amended/rejected
from the draft, so no second model has seen them. Naming them so they are visible as the least-reviewed
part of the plan:

1. **The §1 premise correction itself** — that the file exists and is gitignored. Falsifiable and
   falsified above with `git check-ignore` / `git ls-tree` output; a reviewer can rerun both.
2. **The exact replacement wording in D1.** Nobody but me has reviewed that sentence. It is two lines
   of prose in an ADR References section, and the ai-review sees it in the diff — which is the second
   model, one stage later.
3. **The two-matcher measurement in §3** (35 vs 0). Reproducible; the numbers are the argument.
4. **D2/D3's split** — leave the file ignored, file a ticket. This is the judgement call of the run.
   It is reversible in both directions and takes no position on the answer.

## 6. Unchanged from the draft

DoD, the single-file scope, the red-then-green grep seam, and all three risks stand as drafted.

`risk:low` **re-checked and it holds**: one file, one References bullet, no source, no auth, no money
path, no migration, no CI config. `.gitignore` was considered and deliberately left alone (D2).
Gate 2 is skipped for `risk:low` regardless of the waiver.

→ `agent:plan-review` → `agent:coding`, `Planning` → `Building`.

### Coding done — PR [#124](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/124), commit `0919c7c`

**Implementer: main-agent** (`config.models.implement`), per the plan-final delta. No delegation.

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent
branch: TKT-136-adr-033-dead-citation
base: origin/main @ 8789b1c
commit: 0919c7c
pr: 124
diff: +2 / -1 (1 file)
files: docs/adr/ADR-033-shared-domain-event-envelope.md
local_gate: make check -> EXIT=0, log clean of Error/FAIL/drifted
```

**TDD — the seam was the COS-2 grep, red observed before the edit** (plan-final §2 accepted the
drafter's call to use it rather than commit a checker):

| | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| **red** | `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` | exit 0 — `ADR-033:237` |
| **red** | `git ls-files --error-unmatch docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` | exit 1 — the hit resolves to nothing in the repo |
| **green** | `grep -rn "docs/reviews" docs/` | exit 1 — no hits |
| **green** | COS-1 scan, all 36 ADR files, repo-rooted paths resolved via `git ls-files` | `0 dead -> PASS` |

The COS-1 scan resolves against `git ls-files`, **not** the filesystem — deliberately. The
filesystem is the oracle that would have lied: the cited review file is present locally and
gitignored, so a filesystem-based check goes green on this exact defect here and red only in CI.
That inversion is recorded in the commit message and in TKT-139.

**The diff is the D1 wording from plan-final, unchanged:**

```diff
-- `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` — recommendation R3, the originating finding
+- The 2026-07-25 architecture review, recommendation R3 — the originating finding. The review is not
+  an in-repo document; its recommendations live on the board (R3 → TKT-126, R4 → TKT-128).
```

**Decisions honoured, nothing added:** D2 — `.gitignore` untouched, the ignored review file not
committed. D3 — the discovery filed as **TKT-139** (Backlog): *"`docs/reviews/` is gitignored but
holds a real architecture review — decide whether it belongs in-repo"*, carrying the
`git ls-files`-vs-filesystem trap for any future link checker. D4 — a plain correction, no
`## Amendment` block, since the decision ADR-033 records is untouched.

`risk:low` still holds at the end of coding: 1 file, +2/−1, docs-only, no auth / money path /
migration / CI config touched.

→ `agent:coding` → `agent:ai-review`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ai-review kind=summary -->
### ai-review — **`gpt-5.6-sol`** (`config.models.aiReview`), codex `adversarial-review --base origin/main --scope branch`. Verdict: **approve, no material findings.**

Cross-model pair holds: implementer was main-agent, reviewer `gpt-5.6-sol`. The reviewer was given
the diff and a guilt-primed focus ("assume this diff is wrong and find where"), and **not** the plan
or the reasoning, per the hard rule.

**Judged a PASS on substance, not exit status.** It did not skim — the transcript shows it
independently:

- resolved the branch diff and ran `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`;
- opened the board's own ticket JSON on the `sdlc-state` worktree to check the arrow targets, rather
  than trusting the diff's claim;
- read `docs/reviews/2026-07-25-architecture.md` and located R3/R4 in it;
- confirmed via `git log --all` that the review was never tracked in-repo;
- swept all of `docs/adr/*.md` for comparable citations;
- **rendered the ADR through pandoc as CommonMark** to confirm the two-line continuation still parses
  as one item of the References list — the one real formatting risk in this diff.

### Per-finding verdicts

**Zero findings raised.** The four attacks I pointed it at, and what it concluded:

| Attack | Reviewer's conclusion | My independent check |
|---|---|---|
| Are the arrow targets right — R3 → TKT-126, R4 → TKT-128? | Supported by the board records | **Confirmed before the review ran**, against the review document itself: `docs/reviews/…:60` — *"R3 — Move the event envelope into `shared/go/events`"* = TKT-126/ADR-033; `…:69` — *"R4 — Reconcile ADR-004 with what exists"* = TKT-128, which amended ADR-004 for coverage (`ADR-004:14`). |
| Does the new sentence create its own unverifiable reference? | No — no path, and "not an in-repo document" is true | Agreed; `git ls-tree -r HEAD \| grep -c docs/reviews` = 0 is the proof, and it is in the PR body. |
| Did removing the path lose information the ADR needed? | No durable information beyond the retained provenance | Agreed — and this is exactly why plan-review amended the draft from *delete* to *re-point*: the provenance is what would have been lost. |
| Markdown: does the References section still render as one list? | Yes, CommonMark-verified with pandoc | Accepted on its evidence; this is the check I would most likely have eyeballed instead of run. |
| Does the commit message overclaim? | "Strongly worded but not demonstrably false or materially overclaimed" | Accepted. |

**Incidental → new ticket:** none surfaced by this pass. The one incidental discovery on this ticket
came from planning, not review, and is already filed as **TKT-139**.
**Rejected:** none — nothing to reject.

### Second pass: **not run — one pass, deliberately**

The rule judges the *fix diff*, and **there is no fix diff**: zero findings, zero fixes, so the
branch head after review is byte-identical to the head the reviewer read (`0919c7c`). A second pass
would re-read the same three lines. This is the "pure trivia → one pass" case at its limit — not the
non-trivial case, which requires a blocking fix, changed control flow, a new test, or a materially
changed rebase, none of which exist here. The branch was never behind `origin/main` (`8789b1c` was
still the tip at merge time), so no rebase and no re-green were needed.

### Honest note on the run

The reviewer briefly loaded an unrelated local skill from another client's directory
(`.../MoovAI/moov-skills/...`) — the documented prompt-hijack shape in `references/codex-runner.md`.
It is recorded here because it happened, not because it changed anything: the run went on to return
concrete, repo-cited verification against the intended scope, which the runner doc calls a pass. No
client data crossed into this repo; the read was of a skill file on the same machine.

### Gate 3 — **waived for this run by the repo owner**

The review-guide is posted on PR #124 as the audit record, then the agent squash-merges and deletes
the branch, per the waiver recorded in `kind=claim`. Pre-merge assertion required by the skill —
local `HEAD` must equal `origin/<branch>` — is run and its output pasted into the closeout, so the
merge cannot capture a SHA that predates a local commit.

→ `agent:ai-review` → merge → `PO Review`.
